about: The engineering backlog for autonomous agents. Every entry has a bounded input, a checkable output and at least one command that proves the output. Research and governance tasks live in TASKS.md; this file is code, data, docs and CI only. Validate with: node scripts/agent/tasks.mjs validate

conventions.claim: comment on the linked issue with the task id, or open one with: node scripts/agent/tasks.mjs issue <id>
conventions.done: npm run check && node scripts/audit/a11y.mjs && node scripts/audit/keyboard.mjs

tasks.title: Search overlay: make it a combobox with an announced listbox and Enter-to-open
tasks.why: The palette is a real search but announces nothing and cannot be driven from the keyboard beyond typing.

spec.input: A trimmed query of two or more characters and a search state of idle | loading | ready | error (see SearchOverlay props).
spec.output: role=combobox on the input with aria-expanded, aria-controls and aria-activedescendant; role=listbox with role=option per result; ArrowUp/ArrowDown move the active option; Enter opens the active option through onPick; the result count is announced in the existing polite region.
acceptance: Escape still closes and returns focus to the trigger (keyboard.mjs check 5 stays green).
Focus never leaves the input while arrowing.
The active option is visually distinguishable in both themes.
Render tests cover: no active option before arrowing, wrapping at both ends, Enter calling onPick once.

tasks.notes: Copy is already in locales/{fa,en}/shell.js under search.*. Do not re-add strings to i18n.js.

tasks.title: Principles page: search, filter by light, URL state, one anchor per principle
tasks.why: 113 principles in four tables are readable but not searchable; the anchors exist (principleAnchor) and the coverage filter exists, but a reader cannot address a filtered view.

spec.input: Free text from the reader and an optional light filter (green | amber | red | grey).
spec.output: A search box filtering on principle id, label, title and note in the active language; a light filter beside the existing coverage filter; both reflected in the hash (#/principles?q=...&light=...) and restored on load; the count of matches announced politely; an empty state that names the query.
acceptance: Filters combine (coverage AND light AND query).
Reloading a filtered URL restores the exact view.
No slash ratios, Persian digits through formatNumber, copy in both locales.
Render tests: query narrows the table; light filter excludes the other lights; an impossible combination shows an empty state naming the query.

tasks.notes: parse query with URLSearchParams; keep readRouteFromHash returning recordId for #/principles/<id> and do not break ENG-038's links.

tasks.title: Forms: inline validation, error association and character counters on Levels 2-5 and the bank
tasks.why: A rejected form today reports the refusal in the audit log, not next to the field that caused it.

spec.input: A field value and its rule (minimum length, positive decimal, within budget).
spec.output: aria-invalid on the field, aria-describedby pointing at a message element with role=alert rendered beside the field, the message naming the rule that failed, and a live character counter for the two text fields (proposal title, decision reason).
acceptance: The bank amount field keeps its existing interpret-as-you-type line and its ambiguous-separator refusal (see parseDecimalInput).
Numeric fields reuse parseDecimalInput; no second parser is added.
A submitted invalid form moves focus to the first invalid field.
Render tests cover one text field, one numeric field and one budget field in fa and en.

tasks.notes: Copy goes in locales/{fa,en}/levels.js (sim.*) and bank.js (sim.amountProblem.*), not inline.

tasks.title: Network resilience: request timeouts, cache expiry and an error state that gives a reason
tasks.why: useApi has an in-memory cache with no expiry, no timeout and one anonymous error state, so a stalled request hangs a view forever and a 404 reads like a 500.

spec.input: A path, an AbortSignal-driven deadline (default 8000 ms) and a cache entry with a timestamp.
spec.output: State carries {status, payload, error: {kind: 'timeout' | 'http' | 'contract' | 'network', status?}}; entries older than the TTL are refetched; StateBlock renders a localized sentence per kind and keeps the retry.
acceptance: A pending request is aborted at the deadline and lands in error.kind=timeout.
cache entries expire (default 60 s) without breaking the render tests' primeApiCache seam.
StateBlock's copy exists in both locales and never claims the data is missing when it is only late.
Unit tests with a fake fetch for each error kind.

tasks.notes: Do not add a retry loop or analytics; one retry is a user action in this project.

tasks.title: Route-level code splitting and a bundle budget in CI
tasks.why: Every view ships in one 557 kB chunk; a reader on a slow connection downloads twelve modules to see one.

spec.input: The VIEWS map in App.jsx.
spec.output: React.lazy + Suspense per view with a skeleton fallback that respects prefers-reduced-motion; the hub and the not-found view stay in the main chunk; a build-time assertion that no chunk exceeds 250 kB gzipped except the entry, failing with the chunk's name.
acceptance: First paint of #/hub does not load any module chunk.
Suspense fallback has an accessible name and does not shift the layout.
The budget check is wired into npm run check and CI.
All existing render tests pass (they render App through esbuild, so lazy views must still resolve).

tasks.notes: If lazy loading breaks the SSR render tests, make the loader injectable instead of disabling the test.

tasks.title: Split the 5.7k-line styles.css so parallel UX work stops colliding
tasks.why: One file, 5700 lines, four owners. Every UX PR touches it and conflicts.

spec.input: styles.css, sectioned by the comments already inside it.
spec.output: CSS split into ordered layers under apps/web/src/styles/ (tokens, base, shell, hub, levels, modules, tables, utilities) imported by one entry file in a documented order; @layer used so order is explicit and specificity does not change.
acceptance: Byte-for-byte visual parity: the three audit scripts stay clean at all four widths and both themes.
No selector loses specificity: verified by the audits, not by eye.
The import order is documented at the top of the entry file.
Bundle CSS size grows by no more than 2%.

tasks.notes: Mechanical but risky: do it alone, with no copy or logic changes in the same PR.

tasks.title: Opt-in browser-audit workflow that attaches axe, keyboard and layout output to a PR
tasks.why: The three audit scripts are the evidence for every accessibility claim in the README, but they only run on a developer's machine.

spec.input: A PR labelled ux-audit, or a workflow_dispatch with a URL to the preview.
spec.output: A workflow that installs the browser dependency (see scripts/audit/README.md), boots npm run dev, runs a11y.mjs, keyboard.mjs and layout.mjs, uploads their output as an artifact and posts a single comment with the three results.
acceptance: It does not run on every PR (cost) and cannot block merges by itself.
A failure prints the offending selector and the rule id, not just a non-zero exit.
The workflow has permissions: contents: read and pull-requests: write only.
Documented in scripts/audit/README.md.

tasks.notes: Chromium in CI needs the @sparticuz/chromium extraction described in scripts/audit/README.md.

tasks.title: Migrate one batch of 25 inline { fa, en } strings into the locale files
tasks.why: 462 bilingual literals bypass the locale files, the glossary tests and the parity test, so a missing translation is invisible.

spec.input: Inline t({ fa: '...', en: '...' }, lang) calls in one module.
spec.output: The same strings read from locales/{fa,en}/<module>.js through localeStrings(lang), key for key, with no change to rendered text.
acceptance: Exactly one module per PR (start with Archive.jsx, 59 literals).
No rendered string changes: diff the strings before and after in a script, not by eye.
Key parity between fa and en (localization.test.mjs enforces it).
The count of inline literals drops by the announced number.

tasks.notes: Keep identifiers Latin; run apps/web/test/localization.test.mjs after each batch.

tasks.title: Name the door a library module sits behind, on the twelve library pages
tasks.why: routeMeta names the module but never says that the module sits behind one of the six doors, so a reader in the library loses the map.

spec.input: A parsed route for one of the twelve modules.
spec.output: A crumb between home and the module naming the door it belongs to (module 7 belongs to which door is a data question: add a door field to the module descriptors in i18n.js and mirror it in routeMeta).
acceptance: Every one of the twelve modules has an explicit door in the descriptor table; no module is left unassigned.
Crumbs stay one line at 390 px.
routeMeta tests cover all twelve modules plus the six special views.

tasks.notes: Extend moduleFor/routeMeta in lib/routes.js; do not add a second route table.

tasks.title: Door CTA arrow is a text glyph flipped by CSS: prove it in English (LTR)
tasks.why: ‹ is a glyph whose direction depends on the CSS flip, not on the reading direction; in en it may point the wrong way.

spec.input: The door CTA in fa (RTL) and en (LTR).
spec.output: Either an inline SVG chevron mirrored with logical properties, or a CSS rule that is direction-aware by construction. One of the two, with the reason recorded.
acceptance: Screenshots at 1440 px in both languages show the arrow pointing toward the door in both.
The arrow stays aria-hidden and out of the accessible name.
No new dependency.

tasks.notes: Also check KeyDock's arrows; they share the glyph.

tasks.title: Toasts: pause on focus/hover, and give the theme toggles real names
tasks.why: A toast disappears after 5.2 s while a screen-reader user is still reading it, and the two theme buttons are named only by title (not exposed on touch).

spec.input: A toast with a message, and the two theme buttons in the header.
spec.output: The toast timer pauses on focus and on hover and resumes on blur/leave; the theme buttons carry aria-label and aria-pressed instead of title only, with the visible icon kept aria-hidden.
acceptance: A toast with keyboard focus inside it never disappears.
Both buttons have a name in fa and en; no duplicate announcement of the icon.
Render tests for both behaviours (fake timers or an injected clock).

tasks.notes: Timer control must not depend on wall-clock in tests: inject the delay.

tasks.title: The Bank key shows the rial sign for a toman-denominated unit
tasks.why: One unit is a thousand billion toman; a rial glyph is a 10:1 error printed on the navigation.

spec.input: The bank key in the dock and the bank door in the hub.
spec.output: One symbol and one label for the bank in both places, toman-correct, from the locale files.
acceptance: The same glyph appears in both places (assert it in a render test).
No rial sign anywhere in the rendered interface (grep the payload and the copy).
The accessible name says HMMT, not the glyph.

tasks.notes: The glyph is decorative: keep it out of the accessible name.

tasks.title: Regression guard: no view may lose its h1 when data fails
tasks.why: StateBlock replaced whole views, taking the only h1 with it (axe page-has-heading-one).

spec.input: Every route, with the API cache emptied.
spec.output: A test that renders 19 routes with no data and asserts an h1 inside main.
acceptance: The test fails if a view's error path drops its heading.

tasks.notes: Landed with the hub/level static-hero change; kept here so the guard is discoverable.

tasks.title: Clear the two react-hooks/exhaustive-deps warnings
tasks.why: npm run lint is warning-free except two unstable useMemo dependencies, which means a real re-render churn is hidden in the noise.

spec.input: The two reported sites: Verification.jsx:31 and levels/panels.jsx:113.
spec.output: Each derived value wrapped in its own useMemo (or hoisted out of render), with the dependency array narrowed to what the value actually reads.
acceptance: npx eslint . prints zero problems.
No behaviour change: npm test green, and the Level 1 and Verification render tests unchanged.

tasks.notes: Small and self-contained; good first task for a new agent.

tasks.title: Script that proves every table has a caption and scoped headers
tasks.why: The UX checklist claims captions and scopes; nothing checks it, so the claim will rot.

spec.input: The rendered build at http://127.0.0.1:5173, every route in both languages.
spec.output: A script that fails with file:route, table index and the missing attribute, and passes with a one-line summary; wired into npm run check as audit:tables.
acceptance: Every table in every route is visited, including collapsed disclosures where possible.
Wired as audit:tables in package.json and named in the acceptance of this task, so the claim has a command.
Runs without the browser dependency if it can be done by parsing the SSR render tests' HTML; prefer that, it keeps CI browser-free.

tasks.notes: The SSR path (render tests) is preferred: no Chromium, runs in CI.

tasks.title: Property tests for parseDecimalInput
tasks.why: The amount parser guards a 1000x error and is covered by eleven hand-written cases.

spec.input: A deterministic pseudo-random generator (seeded, no dependency) producing digit strings in the three scripts with separators.
spec.output: Two properties over 2000 generated cases: (1) ok === true implies value > 0 and Number(normalized) === value; (2) an accepted string never parses to a different value when a separator is removed from a grouping-only input.
acceptance: The seed is fixed so a failure is reproducible and printable.
The suite adds under 200 ms.
Any real counter-example found is fixed in decimal.mjs in the same PR, with the case added by hand.

tasks.notes: No faker dependency; a 32-bit LCG is enough.

tasks.title: Derive a principle's light from the audit chain instead of a writable state field
tasks.why: A light that can be written is a claim that can be made; a light that is derived is a claim that can be audited.

spec.input: The coverage records for each principle (surface, evidence, review state) and the audit trail that admits them.
spec.output: A pure function lightFor(principleId, auditChain) with a table of rules, a test proving a light cannot be set without a matching accepted audit entry, and the API rendering the derived value.
acceptance: No route accepts a light as input.
Changing an audit entry changes the light; removing one reverts it.
The 21/47/16/29 distribution is unchanged when the fixture chain is fed in.
Needs maintainer sign-off on the rule table before implementation (open the discussion first).

tasks.notes: Status is proposed on purpose: the rule table is a governance question, not a coding one.

tasks.title: Referendum thresholds are drafts: label them, or source them
tasks.why: A quorum printed without a source reads as a decision that was taken.

spec.input: Every threshold, quorum and gate constant in the referendum payload.
spec.output: Either a source (citation, with the docs/ convention) or the word draft in the payload and on the screen, per constant, with one sentence saying what would make it binding.
acceptance: No number is left unlabelled.
The guardrail script's 'not an election authority' payload assertion still passes.
A reader can tell a sourced number from a proposed one without leaving the page.

tasks.notes: Prefer labelling over inventing a source; an invented citation is a hard stop in this project.

tasks.title: Station readout: the hub's where-am-I-standing logic is dead outside the hub
tasks.why: The label is computed for routes that never render it, which reads as a feature that exists.

spec.input: A route.
spec.output: Either the readout moves into the shell (one line, visible on every route) or the dead branches are removed. The decision is the maintainer's; the implementation is small either way.
acceptance: No branch computes a value nothing renders.
Whichever way it goes, the key dock and the readout agree.

tasks.notes: Blocked on a product decision; ask in the issue before coding.

tasks.title: Charter vs. party: reconcile the README's non-partisan claim with the party layer
tasks.why: Two front-door documents disagree about what the project is. An agent cannot resolve this without a maintainer decision.

spec.input: The README's 'non-partisan' paragraph and the party list in PARTY-AND-PARLIAMENT.md.
spec.output: One precedence statement, in both files, that says which governs and why. No softened language that leaves both claims standing.
acceptance: The contradiction is gone, not phrased around.
The guardrail script's no-government/no-election assertions still pass.

tasks.notes: Documentation-only, but a governance decision: propose wording, do not decide it.
